01 / CHECK THE APPROXIMATION

Released MOLTs reconstruct held-out MLP outputs

We scored layers 17 and 25 on the same 64 UltraChat test_sft conversations, using native Qwen chat formatting and at most 1,024 tokens per conversation. Georg’s MOLT forward implementation and saved normalization statistics were used.

LayerStandardized MSEError reduction vs saved meanMean active gates
170.27125573.43%4.870
250.20173480.59%4.441

Error reduction is 1 − model squared error / saved-mean baseline squared error. It is not answer accuracy. The 95% conversation-bootstrap intervals were 72.21–74.70% (L17) and 79.41–81.78% (L25).

Layer 25 reconstructs better relative to its baseline on this sample. Substantial error remains in both layers. Reconstruction alone does not establish faithful responses to interventions.

Detailed protocol and metrics
02 / A MULTIHOP STARTING POINT

Dallas → Texas → Austin

What is the capital of the state containing Dallas?
Original model: Austin.
Layer 17 replaced by MOLT: Austin

Replacement applied during prompt processing and generation, with no reconstruction-error add-back. Three additional qualitative questions retained the same numerical/geographical answers; the explanation wording varied.

Which representations and transforms activate?

Eight of 73 retrieved Texas-labelled transcoder candidates activated at Dallas. This was a bounded label search, not an exhaustive feature census. On the same original-model inputs, five MOLT transforms activated at Dallas in layer 17 and four in layer 25.

See the Dallas MOLT gates

These activations do not prove the Dallas → Texas → Austin causal path. The MOLT gates were observed without replacing the MLPs.

Response comparison · Transcoder measurements · MOLT measurements
03 / REPRODUCE AN EXISTING INTERVENTION

“Opposite of small” can be steered toward “cold”

What is the opposite of "small"? Reply with only the word, nothing else.

Using the community llm-circuits reproduction, we suppressed six small-associated transcoder directions and added six hot-associated directions. Every edit was at the small token, index 9, across layers 0, 3, 4, 5, 19, 21, and 22.

StrengthTop next tokenOur P(cold)Reference P(cold)
0large1.866e-10%2.785e-10%
1.5large0.002835%0.002521%
2.25cold55.09%54.41%
3cold97.45%96.87%
4.5cold99.77%99.82%
Constrained protocol: attention patterns were frozen across all layers; MLP outputs through layer 22 were pinned to original values plus the selected edits. Later MLPs recomputed normally. At strength above 1, small directions are pushed beyond zero into negative contributions.

The feature IDs and strengths were reused without a new search. The zero-delta control and restored model both matched the original logits exactly. This is a close quantitative reproduction, not a bit-identical one. It measures next-token probabilities, not unrestricted generation.

Full reproduction and selected features
04 / OBSERVE THE MOLT RESPONSE

The intervention changes which gates fire

We captured the original and intervened inputs at layers 21 and 22, then evaluated their MOLT gate encoders separately. These MOLTs were observers; their outputs did not drive the answer. Only 52 MB of gate weights and metadata were needed.

ConditionL21 gates at operandL22 gates at operandTop next tokenP(cold)
Original small43large1.866e-10%
Suppress small33negative0.1252%
Add hot68large1.028e-06%
Suppress + add55cold99.77%
Natural hot33cold97.7%

For the combined edit at layer 21, #202 and #1408 turn on, while #2232 turns off. At layer 22, #40, #61, #71, and #941 turn on, while #55 and #2339 turn off.

Layer 22 gates #71 and #941 also activate on the natural hot prompt, while remaining off for the original small prompt. This is a candidate correspondence, not an established hot label or proof of causal mediation.

At the final prompt position, the combined intervention preserves the active gate sets: seven gates in layer 21 and five in layer 22. Their strengths still change.

Where x and x′ come from: the transcoder edits occur at MLP outputs. A layer’s MOLT input reflects earlier edits, not that layer’s own output edit. Inputs were captured before post-attention normalization, matching Georg’s checkpoint coordinates.
View gate counts across every prompt token

Primary gates use FP32 computation on captured BF16 residuals. The BF16-autocast sensitivity check agrees on active sets at the operand and final positions for every condition; two marginal disagreements occur elsewhere. Only gate behavior was measured here, not transform outputs or Jacobians.

Archive status: Results and code backed up and verified; GPU deletion awaiting required confirmation.

The repository contains the code, measurements, figures, selected feature recipe, source-function hashes, and pinned model revisions. This HTML embeds its figures and explorer data for offline use. Full pretrained weights are intentionally redownloadable rather than committed.

Public GitHub repository · Setup and rerun instructions · Archive status record

Questions still open

  • Do the released Qwen MOLTs match the original MLPs’ Jacobians or finite perturbation responses?
  • What do the candidate layer-22 transforms compute, beyond their gate conditions?
  • Can editing their contributions reproduce the answer change causally?
  • Does a comparable intervention work without frozen attention and pinned MLP outputs?
  • Can this be extended to a validated multihop geography circuit?

No full attribution graph or MOLT-equivalent causal swap has been demonstrated in this session.
